intention: Make the inference ticket RETRIEVABLE and COMPLETE. Two edits at one seam: (a) a reader primitive beside `resolve`/`yield_report` that returns the `inference_calls` rows themselves — by canonical, by ticket, by recency — so the append-only log stops being write-only outside its aggregate; (b) carry the host's RAW RESPONSE BODY on the recorded answer, additively, so a row says what came back rather than what the parse thought to extract. One trailing piece rides the same voyage: a SCAFFOLD line asking the apprentice to say what is wrong with its brief, which becomes worth writing only once (a) and (b) give its answer somewhere honest to land. The bytes UP need no build and this ticket does not build them — `canonical` is already sorted-key JSON of the whole request dict.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: after an apprentice drive, nobody can see what the apprentice was actually told or what it actually said. What exists is `result["response_tail"]` in driver.py — the LAST 4000 chars of the reply — so a long SEARCH/REPLACE edit pushes anything the model said before it off the end, and the ask is not there at all. So a drive that went wrong is diagnosed from a truncated tail and CC's narration of a prompt it assembled but never saw wrapped. MEASURED 2026-08-17 at the cast: every apprentice call already lands a row (interceptor.py:241 routes through domain.resolve), `canonical` already holds every message verbatim INCLUDING aider's own system prompt and repo map, and the readers of `inference_calls` across the whole of cairn/ number TWO — yield_report()'s spent-vs-avoided aggregate and one live.py print. Neither returns a row. AND THE SHARPER WHY: aider_shim's falsifier clause (7) claims nothing enters the prompt that is not traceable to a berthed packet field, and its instrument, `Brief.unsourced()`, audits our spans BEFORE aider wraps them. The claim has always been asserted over half a composite. The wire record is the only place it is checkable, and it was already on disk, unread.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured, and the apprentice's behaviour is currently narrated by a truncated tail and a self-report, neither of which is the call. Law 10 — nothing in the system is immeasurable, and EVERY RECORDED OBSERVATION IS MEASUREMENT: the observation here is already recorded, so this is the ordinary state ('we have not built the measurement yet'), not a claim about the world. Law 7 — a record of truth keeps what arrived; a parse standing in for the body is a presentation surface at a record of truth. Law 1 — the prior-art consult found the ask side already compiled and shrank the build accordingly. Telos 1 is what the same rows already serve via the meter; this makes them answer a second question.
gates: prove_gate: teeth beside the code at cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/, sealed by the tester under netns isolation and persisted through validation_store.persist_validation — the store's own door, never a hand-written trail (a live trouble is on file for exactly that breach). feedback_gate: a red routes to inference_domain's own address; this is an edit at that device's seam, so the origin of a failure here is the domain's parse or its store, never a caller.
falsifier: DONE when all four hold. (a) A caller can name a call and get its ticket back carrying the full request AND the full response body. (b) A recorded miss's `answer` carries the host's body, proved against a host fixture whose body holds a key the parse never extracted — so a build that merely renames the text field cannot pass. (c) A pre-build row lacking the body reads back UNKNOWABLE and never 'empty': absent-not-empty, which is where a hollow green would otherwise hide. (d) The reader round-trips a row's `canonical` to the request dict that produced it, EQUALITY not containment. WRONG INTENT if the retrieved ticket proves not to be what went up — `canonical` is the DRESSED and canonicalized request, and host.py assembles the posted HTTP payload from it, so one assembly hop sits below the record and no row covers it. If that hop carries content, 'every byte up' wants the wire body too and this shape sat one level too high.
horizon: one build for the falsifier. The watch's horizon is ten apprentice-drive tickets pulled back whole, or the first post-build row whose answer carries no body — whichever lands first, deliberately asymmetric. Re-read after the first real apprentice drive whose ticket is read end to end, which is the drive the queued re-chart of aider-builds-a-piece is already going to produce.

distinctions_recorded: THE PRIOR-ART GATE CHANGED THE CAST'S SHAPE, WHICH IS THE GATE EARNING ITS KEEP. The intent was going to BUILD a record of the apprentice's calls; the consult found it already on disk and complete on the ask side, so the build shrank to a reader plus a parse fix. And the thing that would have been re-derived was a WORSE version: anything CC built at the shim would have missed aider's own system prompt and repo map by construction, because the shim never sees them.

A WRITE-ONLY RECORD READS AS NO RECORD, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS TWO. Append-only and complete on the ask side since the device was built; two readers in all of cairn/, both aggregating or printing, neither returning a row. The rows were never missing — the door out of them was. The tell that this is Law 10's ordinary state rather than an absence: it dissolved the moment somebody asked to READ instead of to build.

AN INSTRUMENT CANNOT AUDIT WHAT IT SITS UPSTREAM OF. Brief.unsourced() runs before aider wraps our prompt, so aider_shim's clause (7) has always been asserted over our half of a composite nobody saw whole. Generalises past this seam: any 'nothing enters here but X' claim wants its instrument DOWNSTREAM of the last thing that can add.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MADE THE CAST HONEST. The bytes UP are recorded; the bytes DOWN are parsed and dropped. Recording the response body while waving the request half through would leave the record asymmetric in exactly the direction that hides OUR additions rather than the host's — which is why the assembly hop between `canonical` and the posted payload rides the falsifier instead of the confidence.

THE PIECE THIS CAST STOPPED. A SCAFFOLD span asking the apprentice to report what is wrong was one edit from being built, landing in a 4000-char tail. Akien's redirect — 'the inference domain is supposed to create a inference ticket' — did not reject the piece, it named the record the piece's answer needed. The piece survives, reordered: the ticket first, the question second.

NOT IN SCOPE AND SAID SO: semantic canonicalization (T1.3) and active falsifier invalidation (T1.4), both filed edges on inference_domain's charter, neither touched. This ticket makes the existing rows readable and complete; it does not make them smarter.
